newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's VHI to raise health premiums by nine pct.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's VHI to raise health premiums by nine pct.

text.p: Ireland's Voluntary Health Insurance (VHI) confirmed on Thursday that it is increasing premiums by nine percent from September 1.
VHI acting chief executive Aidan Walsh told Irish state radio that the rise was needed to fund the increasing demands of members and to improve the quality of their lives.
Ireland's largest union, SIPTU, described the increase as "outrageous" and said it was "a new tax by another name".
It blamed an eight million punt increase demanded by the Department of Health for private beds in public hospitals for the rise in premiums.
The VHI said that while the increase was unpalatable, the cost of the medical insurance it provides is extremely low by international standards.
The VHI, which released its annual report on Thursday, recorded a surplus of 1.7 million Irish pounds in the year ended February 28, 1997, against one million the previous year.

The margin by which subscription income exceeded claims rose to 4.6 million from 2.6 million but the operating deficit after charging administrative expenses was 10.5 million, only a marginal improvement on the previous year.
The VHI said a small increase in investment income contributed to the improved surplus while membership increased by 2.4 percent.
